items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to a state transportation
plan

summary: Relates to a state transportation plan; requires such plan include a minimum twenty-year forecast period at the time of adoption, assessing long-range needs spanning such period, including a forecast of highway pavement and bridge conditions; and requires the commissioner of transportation to submit a report to the governor, the temporary president of the senate, and the speaker of the assembly, beginning September first, two thousand nineteen and semi-annually thereafter, a list of those capital projects in the department's capital program that have experienced major schedule changes or major cost changes in letting schedule or construction cost.
title: Relates to a state transportation plan

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 140
 
TO THE ASSEMBLY:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Assembly Bill Number 4880, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  transportation law, in relation to a state
      transportation plan"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This legislation would expand current requirements for the  comprehen-
sive  statewide  master plan for transportation. More specifically, this
legislation would require the  Department  of  Transportation  (DOT)  to
formulate  a twenty year statewide master plan, a 5 year rolling capital
plan, and project programming requirements.
 
  This bill contains a number of technical  flaws.  It  directs  DOT  to
maintain and report on proprietary information pertaining to infrastruc-
ture that is privately owned, financed, operated and maintained. Requir-
ing  the  inclusion of private roadways not under DOT jurisdiction would
necessitate outreach to thousands of local  governments,  which  is  not
feasible  with  DOT's  current staffing levels.  In addition, the legis-
lation overlaps with, and is duplicative of, the  statutory  purview  of
other  transportation  related  agencies  and  authorities. Finally, the
legislation would have an agency estimated fiscal impact of  $1  million
annually.  As  such, it would be more appropriately addressed during the
state budget process.
 
  For the foregoing reasons, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
